newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Central America's debt fell in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: Central America's debt fell in 1996 - study.

text.p: The level of foreign debt among Central American nations fell sharply during 1996, a study published on Tuesday showed.

Net foreign debt among Guatemala, Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica, and El Salvador fell to $17.075 billion at the end of 1996 from $21.264 billion the year before, according to a study by the United Nations' Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (CEPAL) published by a local newspaper.

Nicaragua, the most indebted nation in the region, saw its debt fall the most, from $10.242 billion to $6.108 billion in 1996 largely thanks to debt forgiveness from Russia and Mexico, the study said.
Costa Rica's debt fell to $3.018 billion from $3.217 billion, Guatemala's dropped to $2.054 billion from $2.107 billion and Honduras' debt narrowed to $3.408 billion from $3.466 billion.
The only country in the region whose foreign debt grew was El Salvador, whose debt rose to $2.487 billion from $2.232 billion.
